concepts.description: Naming an emotion in real time, in specific rather than reflexive terms, which both improves the accuracy of the state reading and measurably reduces distress.
concepts.title: Affect Labeling

concepts.description: A trait-like difficulty identifying and describing one's own emotional states, such that internal signals arrive as static rather than a clear reading.
concepts.title: Alexithymia

concepts.description: Validated self-report tools for gauging where a person falls on the alexithymia spectrum, useful for establishing a baseline of how much to trust one's own emotional-state readings.
concepts.title: Alexithymia Self-Report Measures

concepts.description: Automatic next-moment responses to feeling tone — clinging to pleasant, pushing away unpleasant, tuning out neutral — which often run below awareness and distort what a state reading is actually about.
concepts.title: Attachment and Aversion Reactions

concepts.description: Moment-to-moment emotional state is largely determined by what you are attending to right now, so a mood reading taken while attention is elsewhere or split is a different kind of signal than one taken in full presence.
concepts.title: Attention Gates Mood Reading

concepts.description: Operating on habitual autopilot — body doing one thing while mind is elsewhere — lets negative thought fragments coalesce unnoticed until they are too strong to handle easily.
concepts.title: Automatic Pilot Blinds Signal

concepts.description: Recurring somatic patterns — contraction, pushing-away, sudden fatigue — that signal the mind-body has registered something it wants gone, often before the mind names an emotion or admits dislike.
concepts.title: Aversion Bodily Signature

concepts.description: In autistic people, changes in functioning, interests, withdrawal, or repetitive behavior often surface before — or instead of — a clear verbal report of anxiety or depression.
concepts.title: Behavioral Shift as Emotional Signal

concepts.description: A structured technique for reading current physical state by sequentially attending to each part of the body and noting sensations with neutral, non-judgmental descriptors.
concepts.title: Body Scan

concepts.description: Cognitive dulling during burnout or overload — lost train of thought, word-finding failure, weakened imagery — that marks a state shift even when emotion is not clearly named.
concepts.title: Brain Fog as a State Signal

concepts.description: Autistic burnout and clinical depression overlap in fatigue and withdrawal but differ in pleasure capacity, worthlessness, memory, and masking collapse — distinctions that change how much to trust a mood reading.
concepts.title: Burnout vs. Depression State Signals

concepts.description: Deliberately noting what a resting, non-activated body and mind feel like, so that later deviations from it are recognisable as signal rather than treated as the default.
concepts.title: Establishing a Calm Baseline

concepts.description: Reading normal bodily sensations as evidence of serious illness because vigilance and checking amplify attention to sensations that healthy bodies routinely produce.
concepts.title: Catastrophic Sensation Misinterpretation

concepts.description: A persistently elevated sympathetic or reduced parasympathetic baseline that can make "normal" days feel keyed-up and distort what counts as calm.
concepts.title: Chronic Autonomic Hyperarousal

concepts.description: The same sensory stimulus can read as pleasant or unbearable depending on social load, interest, and environment — so stimulus type alone is an incomplete state input.
concepts.title: Context-Dependent Sensory Reading

concepts.description: A structured way to rebuild yesterday as timed episodes and rate feelings per episode, producing a duration-weighted picture of experienced state rather than a single global judgment.
concepts.title: Day Reconstruction Method

concepts.description: An absorbed focus state where sensory input dims and cognitive clarity returns — an autistic-specific alternative to meditation when present- moment body focus lets in overwhelming unfiltered sensation.
concepts.title: Deep Focus as Restorative State

concepts.description: When the emotional reaction to an event surfaces later than the event itself, making a real-time state reading incomplete and retroactive tracing necessary.
concepts.title: Delayed Emotional Processing

concepts.description: Sudden resistance to a task — even one you were about to do — when it is framed as a demand, marking nervous-system fight-or-flight activation rather than simple laziness.
concepts.title: Demand Avoidance as Arousal Signal

concepts.description: A diagnostic check for whether current distress originates externally (sensory overload) or internally (anxiety driven by thought), since the two feel similar but call for reading different signals.
concepts.title: Distinguishing Anxiety from Sensory Overload

concepts.description: Faster unconscious channels — embodied, emotional, and intuitive — register environmental and internal state in milliseconds, while deliberate verbal self-report runs hundreds of times slower, so a conscious "how do I feel?" answer often lags behind what the body already knows.
concepts.title: Embodied Signals Precede Conscious Reading

concepts.description: Emotion is not optional input to good decisions — without felt emotional feedback, even intact reasoning and memory cannot reliably choose or follow through on everyday actions.
concepts.title: Emotion as a Decision Signal

concepts.description: Journaling a single recurring emotion over days or weeks — its physical signature, frequency, and context — purely to observe it and surface trigger patterns, without taking corrective action during the tracking period itself.
concepts.title: Recurring-Emotion Tracking

concepts.description: Metaphorical somatic loci — heart, solar plexus, throat — where attention surfaces constriction or openness tied to grief, vitality, or vocalized emotion, useful when state is felt regionally rather than as a named mood.
concepts.title: Emotional Body Regions

concepts.description: Each emotion tends to produce a distinct, recognisable pattern of physical sensation, which can be used to diagnose which emotion is present by symptom when the emotion's name or origin isn't clear.
concepts.title: The Physical Signature of an Emotion

concepts.description: The observation that pure, single emotions are rare — multiple emotions and physical sensations typically co-occur — which means a state reading usually needs to be decomposed rather than reduced to one label.
concepts.title: The Emotional Storm

concepts.description: Practices for expanding the range of specific words available for naming a feeling, which addresses the "difficulty describing feelings" side of alexithymia separately from the underlying sensing itself.
concepts.title: Emotional Vocabulary Building

concepts.description: When repeated invalidation of felt sensations and needs trains a person to stop trusting their own readings, making even accurate signals hard to believe.
concepts.title: Eroded Perception Trust

concepts.description: Two evaluators inside one person — the self that lives each moment and the self that stores and judges the story — which often disagree and make confidence in a state reading depend on which one is answering.
concepts.title: Experiencing Self vs Remembering Self

concepts.description: Habitual efforts to escape or suppress unwanted emotions, thoughts, and body sensations that disconnect a person from both negative and positive feeling, degrading the quality of real-time state readings.
concepts.title: Experiential Avoidance Signal Blunting

concepts.description: When outward facial display systematically misrepresents felt emotion, degrading both others' readings of you and your confidence that others see what you feel.
concepts.title: Facial Expression Mismatch

concepts.description: Activating smiling, frowning, or head-movement muscles unconsciously shifts emotional judgments — evidence that bodily configuration feeds back into felt state readings the person did not choose.
concepts.title: Facial and Postural Feedback on Judgment

concepts.description: Distinct readable states — burnout, inertia, meltdown, shutdown — with different somatic and behavioral signatures, so telemetry can identify which stress response is forming rather than collapsing them into "stress."
concepts.title: Four Autistic Stress State Signatures

concepts.description: A scanning checklist of four distinct channels to check when reading current state — the outside world, the inside of the body, thoughts and emotions, and a sense of connection to something larger.
concepts.title: Four Corners of Awareness

concepts.description: Awareness of the present moment runs along a graded scale rather than being simply on or off, which matters for judging how much of a current state reading is actually being registered versus missed.
concepts.title: Graded Awareness Model

concepts.description: A sequential daily-habit inventory marked good, bad, or neutral purely for observation — raising nonconscious routines into readable state data without judgment or immediate change pressure.
concepts.title: Habits Scorecard

concepts.description: A four-check screen — hungry, angry, lonely, tired — for whether basic body state is bankrupt before trusting a higher-level mood or decision reading.
concepts.title: HALT Body-Budget Rubric

concepts.description: The same situational theme can produce either a healthy or unhealthy negative emotion; distinguishing them requires reading thinking style, attention focus, and behaviour — not the theme or sensation alone.
concepts.title: Healthy vs Unhealthy Emotion Reading

concepts.description: When a hard question about overall state is unanswered quickly, the mind often substitutes an easier one — usually current mood — and treats the answer as complete.
concepts.title: Heuristic Substitution in State Reading

concepts.description: A heightened sensitivity to other people's emotional states that can register as one's own feeling, making it hard to tell whether an emotional reading originates internally or was absorbed from the surrounding environment.
concepts.title: Hyperempathy and Absorbed Emotion

concepts.description: Deep absorption that blocks hunger, bathroom, breathing, and end-of-day signals until external timers or others notice — making hyperfocus a state that hides load until it is late.
concepts.title: Hyperfocus Bodily Signal Blindness

concepts.description: A brief four-question scan — how things are now, what is in mind, what is in the body, what is skillful — that steps out of automatic pilot before trusting a reactive state reading.
concepts.title: Inquiring Stance Check-In

concepts.description: Feelings, thoughts, body sensations, and behaviors form mutually reinforcing loops where any one dimension can trigger the others — so a partial state reading may miss the cascade already underway.
concepts.title: Interlocking State Dimensions

concepts.description: A single pleasant–unpleasant–neutral scale underlying all feelings that registers the "internal atmosphere" moment to moment and can be read as an early-warning system before specific emotions are named.
concepts.title: Internal Barometer

concepts.description: The body's ability to sense and interpret internal signals — heart rate, breathing, gut sensations, muscle tension, hunger, emotion — which is the raw channel a state reading is built from.
concepts.title: Interoception

concepts.description: Long-term suppression of authentic expression — masking — degrades the reliability of a person's own internal-state reading, both by drowning out natural self-soothing responses and by training people to hide emotion from themselves as well as from others.
concepts.title: Masking Blunts the Signal

concepts.description: The compensating identities performed to hide suppressed traits — humble instead of arrogant, warm instead of cold — which can make the outward presentation a poor guide to internal state.
concepts.title: Masking Personas

concepts.description: Feelings about feelings — guilt about depression, shame about anger — that layer a second emotion on top of a primary one and can block accurate reading of the underlying state.
concepts.title: Meta-Emotions as Signal Noise

concepts.description: A lightweight alternative to a full body scan — folding brief, non-judgmental noticing of a body sensation into an existing routine or a scheduled alarm, for when a dedicated scan is too intrusive or effortful.
concepts.title: Micro Interoceptive Check-Ins

concepts.description: An extreme emotional reaction to specific everyday sounds that most people barely notice, with misperceptions that can make a state reading feel certain when it is actually distorted.
concepts.title: Misophonia

concepts.description: Current mood filters ambiguous facts toward the most negative plausible story, which then feels like evidence rather than interpretation — a calibration hazard when trusting a state reading or its implied cause.
concepts.title: Mood-Colored Interpretation

concepts.description: The implicit "I don't want to feel like this" that keeps the mind in concept-based thinking about feelings rather than reading them directly — a locknut holding rumination in place.
concepts.title: Not-Wanting Locks Rumination

concepts.description: Retrospective judgments of an episode weight its worst moment and its ending heavily and often ignore how long it lasted, distorting confidence in how bad or good it actually was.
concepts.title: Peak-End and Duration Bias

concepts.description: A daily practice of noticing one pleasant moment and recording its thoughts, feelings, and body sensations to tune into valence early and deconstruct experience into readable components.
concepts.title: Pleasant Experience Awareness Log

concepts.description: Verbally naming an action or status while pointing or gesturing at it — engaging eyes, hands, mouth, and ears together to lift behavior from nonconscious autopilot to conscious state reading.
concepts.title: Pointing-and-Calling Awareness

concepts.description: Using physical location and time ("where are my feet right now?") to test whether an anxious state reading corresponds to a problem actionable in this moment, separating present threat from future worry.
concepts.title: Present-Moment Actionability Check

concepts.description: Distinguishes a lifelong trait form of alexithymia from a temporary, situational form brought on by stress, trauma, or burnout, which matters for judging whether a degraded emotional reading is your baseline or a deviation from it.
concepts.title: Primary vs. Secondary Alexithymia

concepts.description: The sense of body position and pressure in space, via muscle and joint receptors, whose over- or under-responsiveness shapes what a person's body is actually signalling about touch and pressure.
concepts.title: Proprioception

concepts.description: Sensitive vulnerabilities from past wounds that amplify a current emotional reaction beyond what the present-moment trigger alone would produce, which matters for judging how much of a reading is genuinely about the present situation.
concepts.title: Raw Spots and Triggers

concepts.description: A rapid, visceral emotional surge triggered by perceived rejection, criticism, or disappointment — often out of proportion to the cue and resistant to slow cognitive reframing in the moment.
concepts.title: Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria as State Signal

concepts.description: A personal, pre-identified set of mind-and-body changes that signal depression may be developing again — established while mood is stable so early warning is possible before escalation.
concepts.title: Relapse Signature State Reading

concepts.description: A pre-agreed phrase, gesture, or code with a trusted person to signal need to leave or get help when meltdown, shutdown, or panic has degraded normal communication.
concepts.title: Safe Word for Overwhelm

concepts.description: Blocking calendar time to deliberately meet sensory avoid and seek needs, because spontaneous self-care often fails when masking and overload consume attention.
concepts.title: Scheduled Sensory Honoring

concepts.description: The added distress fired onto an initial pain or unpleasant feeling — anger, fear, shame, self-criticism — which often hurts more than the first arrow and is identifiable as a separate telemetry channel.
concepts.title: Second Arrow Suffering

concepts.description: The practice of deliberately tuning into inner experience in the moment, used to recover a state reading that masking or interoceptive difficulty has obscured.
concepts.title: Self-Attunement

concepts.description: A strong pull toward specific sensory input — visual inspection, smell, touch, pressure, or repetitive movement — that signals what the nervous system is seeking, not merely what the person "likes."
concepts.title: Sensory Craving

concepts.description: When sensory input registers as too strong, producing avoidance, unusual reactions, or meltdowns — or, critically, only an internal reaction with no outward sign that anything is wrong.
concepts.title: Sensory Over-Responsivity

concepts.description: Building a personal map of sensory triggers (what causes overload) and preferences (what soothes) across taste, smell, touch, sound, and sight, as a baseline against which overload can be recognised early.
concepts.title: Sensory Profile Mapping

concepts.description: During sad mood, the brain's default-mode rumination can actively suppress sensory processing, blunting interoceptive signal and raising depression risk when the shutdown is intense.
concepts.title: Sensory Shutdown Under Sadness

concepts.description: When a sensory stimulus registers too faintly or too late, producing stoicism, accidents, or apparent indifference that can make a state reading look "stable" when internal needs are unmet.
concepts.title: Sensory Under-Responsivity

concepts.description: Coping strategies used to maintain a mask — substance use, eating-disorder behaviour, dissociation, rigid rules, compulsive people-pleasing — that deliberately blunt interoceptive and emotional signal.
concepts.title: Signal-Dulling Coping

concepts.description: A three-part structure for calibrating emotional readings: facts (A), the story the mind adds (B), and the felt reaction (C) — where mistaking B for A is a common source of overconfident state misreadings.
concepts.title: Situation-Interpretation-Reaction Model

concepts.description: A limited pool of social energy that depletes faster under sensory distraction and high-pressure interaction, requiring recovery time alone before state readings stabilize.
concepts.title: Social Calories

concepts.description: Repetitive behavior can be self-soothing sensory regulation or anxiety-driven compulsion; distress to the person doing it — not observer discomfort — is the key discriminator for state reading.
concepts.title: Stim vs. Compulsion Signal Distinction

concepts.description: Repetitive self-stimulation that feels pleasant and reduces stress but often co-occurs with anxiety — a voluntary-yet-compelled behaviour that can flag arousal even when emotion is not consciously named.
concepts.title: Stimming as a State Signal

concepts.description: A structured log of emotional and physical stimuli paired with stress responses over time — scientific-style data collection to reveal which inputs push toward burnout, inertia, meltdown, or shutdown.
concepts.title: Stimuli-Response Journal

concepts.description: The distinct physical and behavioural signatures of the fight-or-flight versus freeze-or-fawn stress responses, useful for recognising that stress is present even when it doesn't look like obvious agitation.
concepts.title: Stress Response Signals

concepts.description: Self-monitoring aimed at social performance — eye contact, tone, stim suppression — that displaces monitoring of internal state and degrades confidence in what is actually happening inside.
concepts.title: Unhelpful Self-Monitoring

concepts.description: A daily practice of noticing one unpleasant moment and recording thoughts, feelings, body sensations, and aversion reactions to tune early warning and deconstruct experience into readable components.
concepts.title: Unpleasant Experience Awareness Log

concepts.description: The inner-ear sense governing balance and movement coordination, whose over- or under-responsiveness explains why the same movement (spinning, swaying, riding in a car) reads as very different signals in different people.
concepts.title: Vestibular Sense

concepts.description: Using deliberate walking attention — formal or informal — as an alternative body anchor when sitting meditation is impractical due to pain, agitation, or anger, keeping mindfulness in motion rather than abandoning state reading.
concepts.title: Walking Meditation as State Anchor
